I farm the same 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I do not start from zero, I start from what has worked on my land. In Quzhou, with well water in hand, I will keep both crops on the full 10.1 mu and push a little on fertilizer rather than risk a weak stand or light ears. I have middle school education and 50 years in the field, so I do look at costs, but I also know losing yield hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the phosphorus in at sowing, give enough nitrogen for tillering and grain fill, irrigate about three times if the season is normal, and keep two pesticide sprays ready because aphids and disease can come fast. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer a bit stronger than wheat because maize eats heavily, irrigate around three times with the well if rain is short, and spray about twice for weeds and insects. I will use rotary tillage because with 10.1 mu and two people at home, it is faster and fits our labor better. I am aiming at steady yield, not gambling on saving a few bags of input.
